title: Strings: bytes, terminators, and safe views
lead: Distinguish std::string, C strings, and string_view, with an explicit ASCII and UTF-8 policy.
why: Names and commands contain spaces, empty lines, and multibyte text. A flawed string model loses data before the algorithm begins.
objectives: Explain: Character arrays and C strings
Implement and verify the lab against its exact contract.
Identify a common defect: Do not retain string_view into a temporary string. Do not call isalpha with a potentially negative char.
prerequisites: Modules 1–2: expressions, comparisons, types, references, and checked cin.
Follow the prerequisite links: cpp.two-dimensional-arrays. New constructs are introduced before the assignment.

concepts.definition: the zero char marking the end of a C string.
a non-owning char sequence with a length.
encoding code points using variable-length byte sequences.
a numeric position in the Unicode code space.
a perceived text unit, sometimes containing multiple code points.
a special no-position value returned by search.

sections.title: Character arrays and C strings
paragraphs: char word[4]{'c','a','t','\0'} is a C string with three letters and a null terminator. char letters[3]{'c','a','t'} is a three-char array, but not a C string. Passing it to a function that searches for \0 violates that function’s precondition.

The array size includes terminator storage; the text length before it does not. An embedded zero byte ends a C string before the buffer ends. Demonstrate the distinction with bounded valid examples, never by executing an unterminated read.

sections.title: std::string owns a sequence
paragraphs: std::string tracks its own char count and may contain embedded \0 data. size() counts chars, not visible letters. c_str() supplies a null-terminated compatibility buffer; do not retain its pointer across string mutation or owner destruction.

operator>> reads a whitespace-delimited token. getline reads a line without its terminating newline and retains internal spaces. Choose according to the format: a project name may contain spaces while a command code may be one ASCII token.

sections.title: ASCII and UTF-8
paragraphs: In UTF-8 one code point can occupy several bytes. Four Cyrillic letters commonly occupy eight bytes, while a perceived character may itself contain several code points. size() promises neither code-point nor grapheme count.

The lab classifies only ASCII A…Z, a…z, 0…9, and ordinary space. Other bytes count as other without modifying the original string. This is an explicit limited contract, not Unicode normalization or collation.

sections.title: string_view does not own
paragraphs: std::string_view from <string_view> holds a pointer and a length into another object’s text. It is convenient for read-only parameters but does not extend a std::string’s lifetime. A view’s substr creates another view; converting to std::string creates an owned copy.

A view need not end in \0. Do not pass view.data() to a C-string API without proving termination. Never return a view into a local string or mutate an owner in a way that may relocate its buffer while the view is in use.

sections.title: Search, emptiness, and byte classes
paragraphs: find returns a position or std::string::npos. Check the result and bounds before substr because the current runtime does not support exceptions. An empty line may be valid under the format; it differs from a failed getline with no line available.

For <cctype>, pass a value representable as unsigned char or EOF; a negative char is invalid. Direct unsigned-char comparisons against ASCII boundaries avoid locale-dependent classification here. An individual UTF-8 byte must not be edited as though it were a whole letter.

sections.title: Text-interface tests
paragraphs: Test an empty line, spaces only, mixed letters and digits, internal spaces, and UTF-8. The lab limit is 200 bytes. Input must contain exactly one line; a second line, even empty, is extra data.

Preserve the original bytes and expected categories without claiming to count human-perceived characters. Next, a struct will group text, numbers, and status into one record without mixing their meanings.

assessment.question: What does size() count in a UTF-8 std::string?
answers: char elements, meaning bytes on the 8-bit-char target
assessment.explanation: Code points and graphemes require a separate algorithm.

assessment.question: Must string_view be null-terminated?
assessment.explanation: A view has a length, not a termination guarantee.

assessment.question: Are an empty line and no line equivalent?
assessment.explanation: An empty line can be read successfully.

assessment.question: What does npos after find mean?
assessment.explanation: Check the result before calculating a substring.

assessment.question: What is needed to accept this lab?
answers: Source, actual results, original tests, and a contract explanation
assessment.explanation: A progress flag is not evidence of independent mastery.
